51322551.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to 6His-tagged EphA4 C204A mutant (29 to 104 residues) (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli Origami 2 (DE3) by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Isothermal Titration Calorimetry: The EphA4 LBD and the peptides were diluted to obtain a final buffer containing 5% DMSO in 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.9, and 100 mM NaCl. The experiments were carried out at 296 K (23°C) using an ITC200 calorimeter (Microcal). Two microliter aliquots of a peptide solution with a concentration between 0.18 mM and 1 mM were injected into the cell containing 205 μL EphA4 LBD at a concentration between 16 μM and 95 μM. Experimental data were analyzed using the Origin software package (Microcal). The integrated values for the reaction heats shown in the lower panels of Figures 1C, 3B and S2A were normalized to the amount of injected peptide after blank subtraction.
original_paragraph.Supporting Figure S2 caption: Supporting Figure S2. The EphA4 E77A mutation does not substantially affect APY-d3 binding affinity. (A) Isothermal titration calorimetry analysis of APY-d3 binding to the EphA4 E77A mutant LBD. Isothermal titration calorimetry profile (upper panel) and integrated values for the reaction heats (lower panel) versus EphA4/peptide molar ratios. Calculated Kd value is shown. This experiment was carried out in parallel with the experiment to determine the Kd value for APY-d3 binding to EphA4 wild-type shown in Figure 1C, while the average Kd value for EphA4 wild-type (from 3 experiments) is shown in Table 2. (B) The APY-d3 N-terminus is located near a large electronegative surface on EphA4. The electrostatic surface of EphA4 WT (red, negatively charged; blue, positively charged) with APY-d3 (cyan sticks) is shown. (C) Electrostatic surface of a model of the EphA4 E77A mutant with APY-d3 (coloring as in panel B). The EphA4 negatively charged surface is largely preserved in the mutant.

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 5% DMSO in 10 mM HEPES, 100 mM NaCl
